ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, administrators and persons exercising effective control must undergo enhanced due diligence per Ley 10/2010 arts. 14 and 32, prior to incorporation and on a continuing basis. Mandatory screening against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iii) Spanish Council of Ministers restrictive measures; and (iv) PEP databases recognized by SEPBLAC. Although OFAC SDN screening is not a domestic Spanish statutory mandate, all servicing credit institutions in Spain de facto require OFAC compliance for USD SWIFT wires and bonded-transfer payment rails, thus OFAC screening is incorporated as a contractual and banking-derived obligation. Adverse matches require filing of a suspicious transaction report (Índice de Operaciones de Riesgo / ROS) with SEPBLAC within 1 business day and blocking of the proposed incorporation process until clearance. Independent checks are documented in the AML/CFT compliance manual of the SL, together with risk scoring assigning Enhanced Due Diligence status due to bonded warehouse wholesale trade and cross-border payment rails (risk tier: Medium_Risk_Enhanced).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), arts. 4, 9, 19-31 and 33-35 (formation, registered office, legal personality, registration); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), arts. 87-95 (name certificate and entry); Ley 38/1992 de Impuestos Especiales for the bonded warehouse activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certificate) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for NIF and excise duties registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (public deed of incorporation) filed with the Provincial Mercantile Registry for registration and legal personality.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Spanish Tax Agency; central portal: www.agenciatributaria.es; centralized registration handled via the Sede Electrónica (electronic office), Censo de Empresarios unit, and provincial AEAT Delegación offices; customs and excise supervision is conducted by the Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: As a precondition, each non-resident shareholder/manager must first obtain an NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) via model EX-01 at the nearest Spanish consulate or national police office. For the SL itself: (1) obtain a negative name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary; (3) file model 036 (Censo de Empresarios) at the local AEAT office to obtain a provisional NIF (letter B for SL) within one month of deed execution; (4) inscribe the SL in the provincial Registro Mercantil; (5) obtain the definitive NIF certificate from AEAT; (6) simultaneously register for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS), IVA (VAT), and Impuestos Especiales (excise duties) by filing model 036 before any commercial activity commences; (7) for bonded wine/spirits trade — apply to the AEAT customs/excise department for authorization as Depositario Autorizado (authorized excise warehousekeeper) and obtain the fiscal depot (depósito fiscal) license, providing an excise guarantee (aval bancario or cash deposit) covering deferred duty; (8) register in the EMCS (Excise Movement and Control System) e-AD digital environment, in the AES (Automated Export System) customs export environment, and, if the bonded stock includes non-EU origin goods, obtain a customs warehouse authorization under the Union Customs Code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a fully resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income at a 25% general rate (15% for newly created SLs for the first two years with positive tax base); no pass-through election is available to Spanish resident SLs; the SL is the separate taxpayer for IVA and excise duties, and its members are taxed only on actual distributions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: (1) corporate tax group consolidation (régimen de consolidación fiscal, art. 61-90 LIS) for groups with ≥70% direct/indirect ownership, requiring a 5-year commitment; (2) reduced-size entity regime (empresa de reducida dimensión, turnover < €10M) granting accelerated depreciation and 10% reinvestment reserve (reserva de capitalización); (3) ETVE regime (entidad de tenencia de valores extranjeros) for full exemption of dividends and capital gains from qualifying non-resident shareholdings; (4) neutrality/merger regime (art. 82 LIS) for tax-deferred intra-group transfers; (5) OSS (One-Stop-Shop) scheme election for distance sales of wine to EU final consumers; (6) EMCS e-AD movement election for excise duty suspension on intra-EU bonded dispatches; (7) optional separate application of the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) reporting calendar for group-consolidated VAT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), Ley 37/1992; parallel excise system — Impuestos Especiales (Ley 38/1992), including Impuesto sobre el Alcohol y Bebidas Derivadas (spirits) and Impuesto sobre la Cerveza; customs duties under EU Union Customs Code (Regulation (EU) No 952/2013) for third-country imports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold: Spain imposes mandatory IVA registration (model 036/037) upon commencement of any economic activity, regardless of turnover level; for non-established foreign suppliers of distance sales to Spanish final consumers, the registration threshold is €10,000 per calendar year of EU-wide distance sales (below which the supplier may remain unregistered unless an OSS election is made); intra-Community acquisitions of goods (other than excise goods) by a non-established business also trigger registration at €10,000 annual threshold; excise goods (wine and spirits) have no acquisition threshold and require immediate Spanish registration when moving under suspension to an authorized warehousekeeper.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance regime: taxpayers with annual turnover > €6M are mandatory SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) filers, transmitting XML invoice records (issued, received, intra-Community, import/export) to AEAT web services within 4 calendar days of issuance (8 days for invoices from non-established suppliers); all Spanish business operators are migrating to mandatory B2B e-invoicing under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and RD 1007/2023 (Veri*factu), requiring certified billing software that generates facturae-3.2 XML invoices with signature metadata and QR-compliance stamp for every invoice issued, including export invoices; bonded operations are separately tracked through the EU EMCS, which requires digital e-AD (electronic Administrative Document) submission and a digital stamping/acceptance event at each dispatch and receipt of wine and spirits under excise suspension.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of wine/spirits to destinations outside the EU qualify for 0% IVA under art. 21 Ley 37/1992, provided the goods physically leave EU customs territory within the statutory dispatch window (the 90-day exit rule) and the exporter retains the transport documents proving third-country arrival; intra-Community dispatches from the bonded warehouse to a VAT-registered EU customer qualify for 0% under art. 25 Ley 37/1992, conditional on the customer's valid VIES VAT identification number being recorded and the recapitulative statement (model 349) being timely filed; in all cases, excise duty remains suspended via EMCS e-AD until proof of export (EX1/AES exit confirmation) or proof of receipt at the EU destination warehouse is lodged with AEAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DUA) submitted through the EU Automated Export System (AES), electronically released by AEAT customs with a validated MRN (Movement Reference Number) and exit-confirmation event

EX-1 copy of the export declaration for excise goods (where required) and the EMCS e-AD (electronic Administrative Document) showing destination status 'Export' with the unique administrative reference code
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill, CMR, CIM) evidencing international carriage from the Spanish bonded warehouse to the third-country destination port/airport
Proof of physical departure from EU customs territory (e.g., destination-country customs entry stamp, transit (T1) discharge evidence, or the AES 'exit' message logged in AEAT records)
For intra-EU zero-rated dispatches: VIES validation printout of the customer's VAT ID, the e-AD movement receipt confirmation, and the model 349 recapitulative statement
Commercial export invoice and Incoterms evidence (EXW/FCA/CPT/CIF) confirming transfer of risk and international shipment instructions

Inward remittance certificate (certificado de entrada de divisas) and bank Swift MT103 statements demonstrating that export proceeds were repatriated to the SL's Spanish bank account within the statutory deadline
Warehouse movement records (salida de depósito) and stock ledger reconciliations linking the dispatch from the fiscal depot to the export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT cross-verifies AES exit messages against EMCS e-AD closures, SII invoice filings, and the bank remittance database; failure to evidence physical exit within 90 days or failure to repatriate export collections within 180 days (Ley 7/2012 presumption of undisclosed income) triggers requalification of the 0% charge to 21% IVA plus default interest (interés de demora) from the supply date, with concurrent Impuesto sobre Sociedades base adjustments; penalties under the Ley General Tributaria (Ley 58/2003) range from 50% to 150% of the under-declared tax for grave infringements (art. 191-192 LGT); fraudulent export schemes — simulated exports, falsified certificates of exit, or circular redemption of bonded goods — additionally trigger excise-duty clawback of the full IIEE assessment, revocation of the Depositario Autorizado authorization and license cancellation, joint-and-several liability of directors, and criminal liability under art. 305 Código Penal (tax fraud over €120,000, punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years); the statutory limitation period for retrospective clawbacks is 4 years (extended to 5 with aggravating circumstances).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European Union single-market framework and the euro area governed by the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange, customs, tax, and anti-money-laundering functions are also administered by the Spanish Ministry of Finance, Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, Dirección General del Tesoro y Política Financiera, and Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has no general exchange-control regime for ordinary current-account or capital-account transactions. Current payments, trade settlements, dividend distributions, interest, royalties, and service fees may generally be paid cross-border without prior foreign-exchange approval, subject to bank AML/KYC controls, sanctions screening, tax withholding, transfer-pricing requirements, beneficial-owner verification, and documentary evidence of the underlying transaction. Capital contributions, shareholder loans, acquisitions, and repatriation of capital are generally permitted without exchange permission, but foreign-investment declarations, Bank of Spain external-transaction reporting, corporate-law approvals, accounting records, and tax filings may apply. Dividend and interest remittances require distributable profits, shareholder and director approvals, solvency and capital-maintenance compliance, and applicable Spanish withholding-tax analysis. Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, unusual intermediaries, cash-intensive alcohol trading, or unexplained circular flows may be delayed or rejected. Bonded alcohol transactions additionally require customs, excise-duty, EMCS, warehouse, and inventory documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank, no general mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline for converting export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the company's commercial discretion, subject to contractual banking terms and accounting requirements. The company must retain commercial invoices, transport and customs evidence, proof of delivery, customer and counterparty records, and evidence supporting any advance, refund, credit note, or third-party payment. Resident entities may have periodic reporting obligations for transactions and positions with non-residents under Banco de España external-sector reporting rules, with frequency generally determined by reportable annual amounts and applicable regulatory thresholds. Customs declarations, VAT treatment, excise-duty records, and EMCS movement records remain mandatory where relevant. Cash physically entering or leaving the European Union at or above EUR 10,000 must be declared under applicable EU and Spanish cash-control rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; optional foreign-currency collection and payment accounts; capital contribution account or escrow-style account only if requested by the bank or transaction structure
Operational Account; foreign-currency account; trade-finance and documentary-credit facilities subject to underwriting
Operational Account; collection account; foreign-currency account; trade-finance account and bonded-inventory cash-management structure subject to approval
Operational Account; foreign-currency account; import-export payment and documentary-credit facilities subject to risk approval
Operational Account; euro and selected foreign-currency accounts; trade-payment services subject to branch and risk appetite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment execution and collections; Low to Medium as the primary treasury bank. A regulated European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution may provide payment accounts, transfers, foreign exchange, cards, and collection services under its authorization and passporting framework. An EMI does not provide a Spanish bank deposit unless funds are separately safeguarded or held with a credit institution, and it may not provide credit or deposit products beyond its statutory permissions. An offshore digital EMI without applicable EU/Spanish authorization, passporting, local agent status, or a compliant correspondent arrangement should not be used for regulated payment services to a Spanish SL. Fintech onboarding may be restricted for bonded alcohol, high-value goods, Latin American corridors, third-party collections, crypto exposure, cash-intensive activity, or complex ownership. A regulated Spanish or EEA bank should remain the principal account for tax, payroll, customs, excise, supplier, and liquidity payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified powers of attorney, and verified corporate records, subject to the bank's policy. Banks may require an in-person meeting or enhanced video interview for non-resident directors, complex or layered ownership, newly incorporated entities, bonded warehouses, high-value alcohol trading, Latin American counterparties, cash activity, foreign shareholder funding, or unexplained payment flows. At least one authorized signatory, beneficial owner, or controlling person may be required to complete enhanced verification. Certified translations, apostilles, legalized documents, and Spanish-language or English-language originals may be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee shareholders, unexplained control rights, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Spanish Commercial Registry extract; articles of association; shareholder register or equivalent ownership chart; passports and proof of address for all beneficial owners and directors; signed ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration; certified corporate resolutions; tax identification numbers; explanation of control rights; and legalized or apostilled foreign corporate documents where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder funding, shareholder loans, or capital injections lacking a clear economic purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder resolutions; executed capital-increase or loan agreement; bank proof of source account; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth memorandum; investor financial statements or audited accounts; tax residence certificates; payment reference identifying capital or loan purpose; accounting entries; and evidence of any required foreign-investment or external-transaction reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value wine and spirits trading inconsistent with the company's size, turnover, storage capacity, or expected payment profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; supplier and customer contracts; purchase orders; commercial invoices; warehouse agreements; customs-authorized or tax-warehouse evidence; excise-duty and EMCS procedures; inventory policy; insurance; transport and logistics contracts; pricing and margin analysis; expected monthly transaction matrix; and audited or management financial forecasts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded-warehouse activity with inadequate proof of title, inventory control, customs status, or excise-duty treatment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Warehouse authorization or contract; customs and excise registrations; EMCS access and movement records; warehousekeeper confirmations; inventory reconciliation; stock-taking reports; bills of lading or CMR documents; customs declarations; duty-suspension evidence; product classification; alcohol traceability records; and documented release, transfer, and destruction controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving Latin America, third-party payers, payment agents, free-trade zones, or jurisdictions classified as high risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-risk matrix; counterparty KYC files; beneficial-owner checks; sanctions and adverse-media screening; written third-party-payment policy; three-way invoice and contract reconciliation; reason for payment; proof of delivery; customs documentation; correspondent-bank details; payment approval records; and enhanced due-diligence report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cash deposits, fragmented transfers, rapid pass-through activity, or transactions inconsistent with normal wholesale settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash prohibition or limitation policy; treasury policy; transaction-monitoring rules; expected-payment profile; customer concentration analysis; bank statements; sales ledger; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; cash-register records where applicable; management explanation; and evidence that settlement occurs through identified commercial counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unrelated third-party accounts, virtual-asset platforms, or offshore accounts for company trade flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal prohibition policy; approved-account list; transaction exception register; counterparty bank-account verification; beneficial-owner confirmation; contractual payment instructions; rationale for any exceptional payment; refund and chargeback controls; and documented remediation plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, customs, or restricted-goods concerns involving alcohol origin, destination, intermediary, vessel, or ultimate customer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening evidence for all parties and transport legs; country-of-origin and product documentation; customs classification; export-control assessment; end-customer certificate; no-reexport undertaking; shipping and vessel screening; beneficial-owner verification; and legal sign-off for higher-risk transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, VAT, excise, transfer-pricing, or permanent-establishment inconsistencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax identification and VAT registration; tax-residence certificates; VAT and excise registrations; tax filings; transfer-pricing policy; intercompany agreements; customs and warehouse records; permanent-establishment analysis; and reconciliation between banking activity, accounting records, customs declarations, and tax returns.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Spanish or EEA bank account held in the SL's legal name, preferably from the investor's own verified account. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding where available and SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies. The payment narrative should identify the legal basis, such as 'capital contribution', 'share capital increase', or 'shareholder loan', and must match the executed corporate documents. Obtain the bank's pre-clearance for significant or unusual funding, provide source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, and reconcile the incoming payment to the capital or loan agreement. For a capital increase, coordinate notarial and Commercial Registry filings, accounting recognition, beneficial-owner records, and any applicable foreign-investment declaration. For shareholder loans, document arm's-length terms, maturity, interest, repayment, transfer-pricing support, and withholding-tax treatment. Do not route capital through personal, unrelated, anonymous, cash, or unregulated virtual-asset accounts. Maintain evidence for Banco de España external reporting, tax audit, AML review, and future dividend or principal repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, preferably confirmed or irrevocable where counterparty or country risk justifies it, for new suppliers, high-value shipments, uncertain jurisdictions, or title-sensitive transactions. Documentary collections, open-account payments, and supplier prepayments should be risk-tiered and supported by purchase orders, invoices, transport documents, customs declarations, warehouse or EMCS records, and proof of delivery. The bank payment reference should identify invoice number, contract, shipment, and beneficiary. For imports, reconcile payment to customs value, Incoterms, VAT, excise, and freight documentation. Apply dual authorization, segregation of duties, beneficiary-master-file controls, sanctions screening, callback verification, and invoice-to-goods-to-payment matching. Avoid third-party settlement unless contractually justified, fully documented, and pre-cleared by the bank. Maintain liquidity buffers for customs duties, excise, VAT, payroll, bank collateral, LC margin, and warehouse charges.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major-currency forwards with an authorized bank, supported by documented forecast or committed commercial exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards where the currency, counterparty, and bank product are legally available and the settlement structure is appropriate; use only for genuine underlying exposure and maintain valuation and collateral records.
Currency swaps for documented funding or cash-flow mismatches, subject to bank documentation, appropriateness assessment, credit limits, collateral terms, and accounting treatment.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for material shareholder loans or bank financing, subject to treasury-policy approval and independent valuation.
FX options and collars for asymmetric exposure protection, subject to suitability, premium, accounting, and maximum-loss controls.
Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency receipts and payments, foreign-currency accounts, supplier-currency negotiation, and settlement-date alignment.

Prohibited or restricted practice: unhedged speculative trading, derivatives without a documented underlying exposure, transactions with unregulated counterparties, and structures that obscure beneficial ownership or circumvent sanctions, tax, accounting, or bank-reporting requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry of the province of the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following approval by the shareholders' meeting; approval must occur by 30 June of the following year (calendar-year accounts).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; temporary closure of the Mercantile Registry for filing of subsequent documents; risk of administrative strike-off after two consecutive years of non-deposit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the tax year end; for calendar-year taxpayers by 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharges plus late-payment interest; penalties up to 20% of the undeclared tax; liability to administrative tax assessment and coercive collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ultimate beneficial owner confirmation (Declaración Anual de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Registro de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the annual accounts filing; for calendar-year companies no later than 30 July of the following year; changes during the year must be declared within 10 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 600 to EUR 5,000 per omitted or false UBO declaration under anti-money-laundering law; possible blocking of shareholder resolutions in the Mercantile Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bonded warehouse excise duty annual recapitulative statement (suspension regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT - Oficina Nacional de Gestión de Impuestos Especiales (alcoholic beverages administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly intra-Community excise returns and annual recapitulative declaration filed by 30 January of each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Excise duty assessment plus monthly surcharge of 5% to 20% depending on delay; penalty of EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 for late declaration; suspension authorization may be revoked and the bonded warehouse closed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit if, for two consecutive years, the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total assets EUR 2,850,000; net turnover EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) as approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007; IFRS-EU mandatory for companies that form part of a group filing consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain an internal register of ultimate beneficial owners and file an annual confirmation with the Registro Mercantil Central. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the shareholders' register and reported to the Mercantile Registry within 10 days of the change; the annual confirmation updates all UBO entries as of the close of the prior fiscal year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created SLs during the first two tax years in which positive taxable income is obtained, excluding asset-holding companies; R&D and technological innovation credits (25% base, 42% incremental); job-creation credit of EUR 250-EUR 750 per new indefinite contract; Canary Islands ZEC preferential regime; internationalisation deduction for eligible overseas expenses; indefinite tax-loss carryforward with annual offset limits of 70% (turnover under EUR 20 million), 50% (EUR 20-60 million) and 25% (EUR 60 million or above), subject to a minimum EUR 1 million offset where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 - Declaración del Impuesto sobre Sociedades: AEAT electronic filing via Sede Electrónica (www.agenciatributaria.es) with electronic certificate (software compatible DES / win32).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Quarterly advance payments are filed separately on Modelo 202 (April, October, December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 25 calendar days following six months after the fiscal year end. For a calendar-year SL, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 001 - Only the Spanish NIF of the SL
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification field: SL fiscal identification number, corporate name, tax domicile, CNAE code 4632 for bonded-wine and spirits wholesale, and licence data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not entities on Modelo 200. The SL files as a resident corporate taxpayer. The box must contain only the Spanish NIF of the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting period start and end dates, normally 01/01 to 31/12, with amount in euros unless a shortened period due to incorporation or cessation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident data is entered. The fiscal year matches the SL accounting year; foreign parents are reported only on their own Spanish CRS/NR forms if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net pre-tax profit or loss according to the statutory financial statements, including bonded inventory valuation adjustments, logistics costs, and dutiable warehouse revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident owner's accounting treatment is irrelevant; Spain requires the SL's audited Spanish GAAP accounting result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying permanent and timing adjustments: deductible expenses, tax-exempt items, losses carried forward, transfer-pricing corrections, and anti-abuse recharacterisations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with the non-resident shareholder must comply with Spanish transfer-pricing rules; corresponding adjustments require arm's length substantiation in euro or reporting-currency equivalent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax levy after statutory tax credits, double-tax relief, withholding credits, and instalment payments. The resulting amount is either to pay or to claim as a refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a DTA applies to any cross-border income item, the DTA claim form and Tax Residence Certificate must be attached to the Modelo 200 tax file and reflected in the appropriate credit boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 006 - Declaración informativa de operaciones con terceros
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual related-party transaction declaration reporting cross-border and domestic related-party dealings (Modelo 232 is required for transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 in a tax year).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All non-resident counterparties must carry the NIF or foreign tax identification number in the declaration. Failure to file or incomplete data generates fixed penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Modelo 200 without prior tax authority demand triggers surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 3-6 months, 15% within 6-12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. If AEAT demands a return, the penalty is 50% of the amount due (reduced to 25% with conformity). Failure to file a return with no tax due incurs a fixed fine of EUR 200, increased for large companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 - Pago fraccionado del Impuesto sobre Sociedades: AEAT electronic portal, same Sede Electrónica authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly advance tax payment submitted three times per fiscal year (usually by 20 April, 20 October, and 20 December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline for each instalment is the first 20 calendar days of the months of April, October, and December for a calendar-year taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL is the only taxpayer; non-resident shareholders have no instalment obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 002 - Clave de modalidad (a / b / c)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select method: (a) 18% of the tax owed on the previous year's taxable base, (b) 18% on the positive taxable base of the periods elapsed, or (c) 25% for entities with net turnover of at least EUR 10 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A newly formed SL owned by non-residents may use the reduced method only when permitted under Article 40 LIS; otherwise the standard 18% rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount to pay or to carry back, net of prior instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments are paid on behalf of the future Modelo 200 liability; non-resident parent loans or funding are not treated as instalments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to present Modelo 202 incurs the same Article 198 LGT sanction regime: a fixed fine of EUR 200 for zero liability and surcharge/penalty on the amount not paid, plus late-payment interest from the statutory deadline. Directors can be personally liable if they ordered the concealment of taxable activity.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax Act (IRNR) for distributions to non-resident shareholders that do not qualify for a reduced treaty rate. No additional Spanish corporate dividend tax is imposed on the distributing SL.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver, before the distribution date, a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of its country of residence and, where required, complete Spanish Form 210 for refund claims. The Spanish payer may apply the reduced rate at source only if the DTA protocol permits and the TRC evidencing beneficial ownership is retained in its records. If the payer withheld the statutory 19%, the shareholder may claim a refund by filing Form 210 with the AEAT within four years after the payment, attaching the TRC and proof of effective taxation in the residence country. An annual informative return, Form 216, reports all non-resident distributions and withholdings to the tax authorities. Non-resident corporate shareholders must in addition obtain a Spanish NIF for non-residents (NIF-No resident) or, for EU residents without a Spanish establishment, use their state VAT number where recognised.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding for royalties and interest paid by the Spanish SL to non-resident beneficial owners is 19% on gross amounts. Treaty rates vary: the Spain-US treaty generally provides 10% on interest and royalties; Spain-Germany typically reduces interest to 0% and royalties to 5%; Spain-UK provides 0% on interest and 10% on royalties. A DTA normally applies only when the non-resident owner is the beneficial owner and meets the limitation-of-benefits clause. For intra-group royalty or interest payments, the payer must certify the arm's length character and apply the applicable DTA form before making the payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10 million annual net turnover triggers the mandatory Local File (documentación del contribuyente). EUR 45 million consolidated group net revenue triggers the Master File (documentación del grupo). Transactions with related parties exceeding EUR 250,000 also require documentation for taxpayers below the turnover threshold. Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR) files are mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more. For an ES_SL engaged in bonded wine and spirits trade, any cross-border purchase/sale with the foreign parent, logistics arrangements, and trademark licensing arrangements above the threshold must be contemporaneously documented in Spanish and English.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime in the Gulf Cooperation Council style. Substance is nevertheless enforced through the General Anti-Abuse Clause (Article 15 LGT), the corporate residency rules (management and control in Spain), CFC rules, the beneficial-ownership requirement under tax treaties, and the anti-money-laundering substance checks. For an ES_SL in bonded trade, the company must maintain licences, physically operated bonded warehouse facilities, inventory records, staff or contractual personnel in Spain, bank accounts, and effective management decisions locally, so that the Spanish entity is not viewed as a letterbox or conduit. In tax audits, absence of these substance elements will trigger recharacterisation of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, and joint liability of directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Defraudación Tributaria (Corporate Income Tax)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income from bonded wine and spirits sales, such as off-book cash receipts, false purchase invoices, fictitious logistics costs, secret commissions, or sham distribution structures designed to shift profit to low-tax offshore entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalty from 50% to 150% of the defrauded quota under Article 183 LGT, plus late-payment interest. Criminal prosecution under Article 305 of the Código Penal when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000: imprisonment from 2 to 6 years, a fine of between double and sextuple the defrauded amount, and loss of tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto administrators face joint, several, and unlimited liability under Articles 36, 42 and 43 LGT; the corporate veil can be pierced by civil courts, exposing personal bank accounts, properties and shares. In criminal cases the court may impose a travel ban, provisional detention, and assets embargo, and directors who directed or knowingly benefited from the fraud are co-principals for the full tax liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-preparation, incomplete filing, or deliberate submission of false transfer-pricing documentation and arm's-length files for cross-border purchases of Scotch and Bordeaux wine, warehouse fees, or trademark royalties, particularly when the transactions are with the non-resident shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 18.8 LIS and Article 198 LGT, each omitted, false, or inaccurate datum in the TP file triggers a fixed fine of EUR 1,000, with a cap of EUR 15,000 per infraction. Failure to provide the documentation when formally requested also permits AEAT to recharacterise transactions and adjust taxable income upward, increasing the tax base and generating penalties of 50%-150% on the understated amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The statutory administrator who signs the Tax File and knowingly presents incomplete TP documentation is jointly liable for the resulting tax debt under Article 43.1.b LGT. In egregious cases, the TP failure is treated as a criminal evasion predicate, which can lead to imprisonment and asset forfeiture of the director who knowingly created non-arm's-length pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Letterbox Structure and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an SL with no real economic activity in Spain, no bonded warehouse licences, no physical inventory or employees, and using it solely as a routing entity to obtain Spanish tax certificates, EU excise movement benefits, or treaty-based withholding reductions for wine and spirits dividends, royalties, or interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the General Anti-Abuse Clause (Article 15 LGT) and the doctrine of abuse of law, the Tax Agency recaptures the full tax difference plus 50%-150% penalty and strips the treaty benefits. Infringement of DAC6 hall-of-shame reporting obligations carries fines of EUR 2,000 per arrangement (EUR 4,000 if the director is an intermediary), and repeated use of sham vehicles may lead to corporate dissolution under Article 363 LSC for economic inactivity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell SL are personally liable for tax debts when they have resigned without liquidating, or when the SL was entrusted with assets and the director used it to defraud creditors. The corporate veil is pierced: civil responsibility extends to the director's personal estate. A travel ban and prohibition from managing Spanish entities can be issued concurrently with criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Excise Fraud in Bonded Trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using bonded warehouse operations to commit excise fraud through double invoicing, smuggling, non-existent customs entries, cash structuring of wine and spirit payments, or financing third-party money laundering through false export and re-import operations. Also, failure to file suspicious transaction reports with SEPBLAC or not appointing a compliance officer when the scope qualifies under Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Serious AML infraction under Article 51 of Law 10/2010 carries fines from EUR 90,000 to EUR 450,000; very serious infractions exceed EUR 450,000. Criminal money laundering under Article 301 Código Penal is punishable by 6 months to 6 years of imprisonment plus fines. Customs/excise fraud is separately sanctioned by EU Regulation and the Spanish excise duty code with a 150% penalty and confiscation of the bonded goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and de facto managers are personally liable for administrative AML fines if they designed or consented to the defective compliance system. Under Article 42.1 LGT, the director who manages the flow of illicit money can be held jointly liable for the SL's tax debts. The criminal court may issue a travel ban, extradition, asset freeze, and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced, and the personal assets of directors are used for civil restitution of the wine/spirits and associated profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SL distributes dividends to a non-resident parent or shareholder and fails to withhold the 19% IRNR, or recategorises a dividend as a reimbursement of debt, a loan, or a reduction of capital to evade the withholding obligation. Also, invoking a DTA without a valid Tax Residence Certificate in circumstances constituting fraudulent use of a treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SL as payer is jointly liable for the unwithheld tax plus late-payment interest. The withholding failure triggers a penalty of 50% of the omitted tax under Article 191.3 LGT, and the non-resident shareholder is taxed on the full gross distribution. If the evasion exceeds EUR 120,000 in a single fiscal year, criminal tax evasion sanctions apply: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years or up to 6 years where the damage exceeds EUR 600,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally signed a distribution without withholding are jointly and severally liable under Article 42.2 LGT. In criminal proceedings against the company, the court can impose a personal deterrent bond, prohibit departure from Spanish territory, and imprison the director; piercing the corporate veil permits seizure of the director's personal assets to pay the restitution owed to the Spanish Treasury.
